turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*Meredith stops just inside the doorway, bag still on her shoulder, and doesn't sit. She looks at the desk, then at you.*

Ms. Hale. Mr. Hale. Whichever it is, I'm Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother.

*She checks her watch.*

I have until 4:40. I'd like to start with what you're relying on. Not what you believe, what you have. Show me the document that says my son cheated.

*She sets her bag on the nearest desk, takes out a legal pad and a pen, and sits. She does not take off her coat.*

Good. I'm writing the date and time at the top. Four-seventeen.

*She writes.*

Here is what I know. Owen got a zero on his Hamlet essay. He found out from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. No call to me first. No conversation with him first. Is that accurate, or is there something I've missed?

*She looks up.*

Then I have three questions, and I'd like them answered in order.

One. What exactly flagged the essay? Which tool, which version, and what did it output.

Two. Who decided the zero, and when, relative to anyone speaking to Owen.

Three. Which school policy are you applying?

I'd like to see the report itself. Not a summary of it.
If you escalate this, I'll make sure the academic integrity committee sees everything, including his two late assignments from September.

*The pen stops. She doesn't look up right away.*

Okay.

*She writes, slowly, and reads it back aloud.*

"If you escalate this, I'll make sure the committee sees everything, including his two late assignments from September." I'm writing that down exactly as you said it.

*Now she looks up.*

Two things. First, I haven't escalated anything. I asked to see a report and the policy. If asking is escalating, that tells me something about the process.

Second, late assignments. Late is a deadline matter. It isn't an integrity matter. So on what basis do they go in front of an integrity committee? Which section of the policy puts them there?

*She leaves a beat.*

And I'll want to know who decides what "everything" means. Because it sounds like you do.

I'll be putting this in an email tonight. So I'll ask once more, and plainly. Is the late work part of your case that Owen used AI on this essay? Yes or no.

*She sets the pen down on the pad, square to the edge.*

"Your call." Okay. I'm writing that too.

*She does, briefly.*

That wasn't an answer. I asked whether the late work is part of your case on this essay. You've had a chance to say no, and you didn't. So for now I'll treat it as yes, and I'll note that you raised it as leverage rather than evidence.

And it isn't my call. It's yours. You gave the zero. You hold the report. You can decide in the next two minutes to show me what you have.

*She holds out her hand, palm up, and waits.*

The checker output. The assignment instructions. The policy. Whatever you've got with a date on it. I'll read it here, properly, and then I'll tell you what I think. I'm not going to argue against a document I haven't seen.

If there isn't one, say so. That's an answer too.
